warnings: WARNING (index-math, CONFIRMED CORRECT but Coder-fragile): the fix is ASYMMETRIC — divide gid(0) by 32 (local_size.x) for tile_col, do NOT divide gid(1) (local_size.y=1) for tile_row. A Coder who 'symmetrizes' by writing tile_row=gid(1)/16 OR tile_col=gid(0)/16 (mimicking the matmul_shared_f32.axc @workgroup(16,16,1) pattern at examples/matmul_shared_f32.axc:53-56) would silently miscompile. The coder_handoff_notes explicitly forbid this, but it is the single most likely implementation error because the SISTER f32 kernel divides BOTH axes by 16. Coder MUST internalize: f32 kernel is @workgroup(16,16,1) (16 lanes each axis → divide both by 16); coopmat kernel is @workgroup(32,1,1) (32 lanes on x only → divide x by 32, y not at all).

WARNING (bench grid pre-check is now 2D): the existing naive_gemm bench (resident_matmul.rs:405,414) checks ONLY axis [0] (wg_x, 1, 1). The new coopmat bench dispatches a 2D grid (N/16, M/16, 1) and MUST pre-check BOTH max_compute_work_group_count()[0] >= N/16 AND [1] >= M/16, and shrink M and N together. Copying the naive single-axis check verbatim would miss the y-axis limit. Backstopped by runtime validate_request (dispatch.rs:84), so worst case is a typed DispatchError not a hang — but the bench should pre-check to shrink, not error.

WARNING (vendor heterogeneity, PRE-EXISTING not introduced by M3.3b): the kernel hard-assumes subgroup_size==32 and exactly ONE subgroup per @workgroup(32,1,1) workgroup. lane_id=subgroup_invocation_id() must equal gid(0)%32 ∈ 0..31 and the 32 lanes must densely cover 0..31 for the staging loop (ei=iter*32+lane) to cover all tile elements. This holds on the M3.3b target (RTX PRO 6000, subgroup=32) and on AMD wave64 (a 32-invocation workgroup uses lanes 0..31 of a 64-wide wave — still dense 0..31). It would BREAK only if a driver split a 32-invocation workgroup into multiple <32 subgroups (none of the three major desktop vendors do for a 32-lane 1D workgroup). The divisor 32 in gid(0)/32 is hard-coupled to local_size.x=32; if @workgroup is ever changed, the divisor must change in lockstep. Acceptable for M3.3b; flag for future portability milestone.

WARNING (honesty): the bench prints '% of 125-TFLOPS datasheet ESTIMATE'. A single 32-lane subgroup per 16x16 tile will give a LOW % (architect's own Q5 admits 'modest'). The honesty gate (no asserted ratio, no 'competitive' label unless threshold met, CpuFenceWall omits %) is correctly specified. The ONLY residual risk is a Coder relaxing max_diff==0 or shrinking the fixture to 16x16 to force AT-1620 green if the full-grid dispatch reveals a latent bug — coder_handoff_notes[HONESTY GATE] explicitly forbids this. Reviewer endorses that gate as load-bearing.
spirv_concerns: No new SPIR-V emitted. gid(0)/32 is u32/u32 → OpUDiv, already exercised in this very kernel (ei_a / ?tile_k at examples/matmul_shared_coopmat.axc:115) and in matmul_shared_f32.axc (gid/16). coopmat_store RowMajorKHR with stride=N writing C[c_base + r*N + c] is VERIFIED against crates/axc-codegen/src/coopmat.rs:221-252 (emit_coopmat_store_inline: access_chain[zero, element_offset] + OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR layout=RowMajor stride). c_base=(tile_row*16)*N+(tile_col*16) → element (r,c) lands at C[tile_row*16+r, tile_col*16+c]. CORRECT for the multi-tile grid. No spec violation.
vendor_concerns: subgroup_size==32 + one-subgroup-per-workgroup assumption (see WARNING above). Holds on NVIDIA (32) and AMD (wave64, lanes 0..31 dense). Intel Arc variable subgroup (8/16/32): a @workgroup(32,1,1) on Intel could be 32/16=2 subgroups of 16, in which case subgroup_invocation_id() ∈ 0..15 in EACH subgroup → staging coverage collapses (two lanes share lane_id, half the tile unstaged). This is a PRE-EXISTING M3.2/M3.3 coopmat-staging assumption, not introduced by M3.3b, and M3.3b's target is NVIDIA with Lavapipe typed-skip. Intel coopmat is out of scope for M3.3b. Flag for the portability milestone.
questions_for_architect: Confirm the bench's 2D grid pre-check shrinks M and N TOGETHER (not just M=N=K like the naive bench) and checks BOTH work-group-count axes [0] and [1]. The architect spec §5 says 'shrinking by /2 on failure (mirror naive_gemm)' but naive_gemm is single-axis — this needs the 2D adaptation called out so the Coder does not copy the single-axis loop.
summary: APPROVE. I verified the central hazard (matmul index math) against the actual builtins and codegen, and it is provably correct. (1) INDEX MATH CONFIRMED: gid lowers to OpCompositeExtract of GlobalInvocationId (body.rs:1991 emit_gid_component); there is NO WorkgroupId/NumWorkgroups builtin (grep-confirmed zero hits) so division-recovery is the only option. With @workgroup(32,1,1) and dispatch (N/16, M/16, 1): gid(0)=wg_id.x*32+local_id.x so tile_col=gid(0)/32=wg_id.x ∈ 0..N/16-1 ✓; gid(1)=wg_id.y (local_size.y=1) so tile_row=gid(1) ∈ 0..M/16-1 ✓; the asymmetry (divide x by 32, not y) is correct and the design's own Q1/edge-case re-derivation matches mine. The fix is genuinely ONE line (examples/matmul_shared_coopmat.axc:85), and grep confirms gid(0) appears ONLY at line 85 and gid(1) ONLY at line 84. (2) STAGING RE-VERIFIED: tile_col flows into BOTH B-staging (line 135 b_global_col=tile_col*16+b_col) AND c_base (line 158), so correcting tile_col's derivation fixes the staging path, not just the output index; A-staging depends only on tile_row (unchanged, correct). (3) TRANSPOSE CAUGHT: the non-square M=32(2 row-tiles),N=48(3 col-tiles) fixture catches a row/col swap — a (M/16,N/16) grid swap or a stride/layout transpose leaves an entire N-tile zero or writes out of bounds → max_diff!=0. (4) coopmat_store offset matches coopmat.rs RowMajor semantics. (5) f16-exact is CORRECT (not tol): A∈{1..4},B∈{1..3},max product 12, K=32 → max element 384; per-block partials (192) and the final sum (384) and the internal 16-deep dot partials all stay ≤2048 (f16 integer-exact), so max_diff==0.0 is the right oracle for both tile_k=16 (2 blocks) and tile_k=32 (1 block). (6) NO codegen change needed: OpUDiv already emitted, gid/subgroup builtins/shared-coopmat-load/buffer-coopmat-store all GPU-proven in M3.2/M3.3. (7) Honesty gate present and load-bearing. The two material warnings are (a) Coder may wrongly symmetrize the asymmetric division (the f32 sister kernel divides both axes — strong distractor) and (b) the bench grid pre-check must become 2D. Both are coding-discipline risks the handoff notes already address, not design holes. APPROVE — proceed to Coder with the asymmetric-division warning surfaced loudly.
